title: Dementia: type, stage and behavior
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's cognitive disorder.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for memory loss and cognitive decline.

HPI
The patient is a 73-year-old male presenting today for a scheduled follow-up regarding his Alzheimer's disease. He is accompanied by his primary caregiver. The caregiver reports that the patient remains stable at home and is generally well-behaved. There are no concerns regarding his behavior or mood during this period. The patient is calm and cooperative during the evaluation. He continues to require significant assistance with activities of daily living.

Medication List
Donepezil 10mg daily
Memantine 20mg twice daily

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented to person only. He is cooperative and pleasant. Speech is clear but limited in content. He is able to follow simple commands. No physical distress noted.

Assessment
The patient has a diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease. At this time, he is presenting with severe dementia. He remains stable on his current pharmacological regimen with no acute behavioral issues noted.

Plan
Continue current medications for Alzheimer's disease and severe dementia. Caregiver was advised on safety measures and supervised care. Follow up in three months.

Electronically signed
H. Tanaka, PA-C
May 14, 2026
explanations: Alzheimer's disease: G30.9, sequenced first; the dementia is then coded with F02.- (dementia in other diseases classified elsewhere).
Alzheimer's disease (F02.-, dementia in other diseases), severe, without behavioral disturbance: F02.C0.

distractors.why: F02.- is a manifestation code: code first the underlying Alzheimer's disease (G30.9).
The provider documents the stage (severe): it decides the code and the HCC.
Dementia due to Alzheimer's disease is F02.- (in other diseases), not F03.- (unspecified dementia).
